author: Michael Larabel
description: Just shy of two weeks since a dozen vulnerabilities were published for the X.Org Server and XWayland, more than one dozen vulnerabilities were made public today affecting multiple X.Org client libraries...
title: 17 More Security Vulnerabilities Made Public For X.Org Libraries

author: Michael Larabel
description: The GNOME OS Linux distribution to date has just been in GNOME OS Nightly form for tracking the latest nightly packages of GNOME in their current development form. GNOME OS Preview was announced today as their trek toward a stable GNOME OS in using the latest GNOME stable releases rather than nightly form...
title: GNOME OS Preview Announced In Road Toward A Stable Release

author: Michael Larabel
description: The Linux 7.3 kernel is slated to be officially released on Sunday, 18 October, barring any last minute issues from coming about. With that said, here's a reminder about some of the most exciting features to look forward to in this next kernel version...
title: The Best Features Of Linux 7.3: Performance Improvements, Lots From Valve

author: Michael Larabel
description: Longtime Linux kernel engineer Darrick Wong who stepped down as the XFS file-system maintainer in 2023 is now taking a step back from his other Linux kernel development roles after working on the kernel the past 23 years...
title: After 23 Years, Longtime Linux Developer To "Step Back For A While"

author: Michael Larabel
description: It's been nearly one year since receiving the Gigabyte R284-A92-AAL1 2U Granite Rapids server platform for continuing my testing of the flagship Xeon 6980P processors. Curious how the Xeon 6980P 2P performance has evolved on Linux since then, I ran some benchmarks on the newly-released Ubuntu Server 26.10 against the tests carried out last year on Ubuntu 25.10 with the same hardware.
title: Intel Xeon 6980P Granite Rapids Performance On Linux Over The Past Year

author: Michael Larabel
description: Starling, the open-source desktop environment written in Swift and with its own Wayland compositor too and written largely via Claude Code, has now rolled out its own AI-generated office suite...
title: AI-Generated Starling Desktop Environment Rolls Out Its Own Office Suite

author: Michael Larabel
description: The RPM v4 packaging format has been used by Red Hat Enterprise Linux and Fedora and its derivatives for more than two decades. With next year's Fedora 46 release, Fedora Linux may finally transition to the modern RPM v6 packaging format...
title: Fedora 46 Looking At Moving To RPM v6 Package Format

author: Michael Larabel
description: With pending code for Mesa, the LLVMpipe software-based Gallium3D/OpenGL driver could soon become faster on modern systems that support AVX-512. That's assuming the AI/LLVM-generated code is all in order...
title: AI Resurrects AVX-512 Support For Mesa's LLVMpipe Software Driver

author: Michael Larabel
description: Linux 7.4 is enabling support for a new Intel CPU feature for providing safety against possible denial of service attacks using Trust Domain Extensions "TDX" VMs. The new feature is Intel Instruction Timeout and previously in-development known as Notify VM Exit...
title: Linux 7.4 To Enable Intel Instruction Timeout For Fending Off TDX VM DoS Attacks

author: Michael Larabel
description: Intel software engineers today released the latest version of LLM-Scaler-vLLM PV 1.5, their containerized Docker stack providing a convenient AI/LLM experience atop Intel Arc Graphics hardware and born out of their Project Battlematrix initiative...
title: Intel LLM-Scaler-vLLM PV 1.5 Brings Big Improvements

author: Michael Larabel
description: Merged today to Mesa 26.3 is initial video acceleration support for the generic Zink Gallium3D driver built atop the Vulkan APIs. What this implementation allows is exposing Video Acceleration API (VA-API) implemented atop the Vulkan Video interfaces...
title: Mesa's Zink Now Offers VA-API Video Acceleration Atop Vulkan Video
